metadata.title: Command line — Gazetta
metadata.description: Every gazetta command and flag, site and target auto-detection, ports, CI behaviour and exit codes.

components.name: docs-cli-body
components.content:
> These docs describe Gazetta's `main` branch. The latest release on npm, 0.8.0, is older and works differently in places, and it lacks security fixes made since. To follow these docs, [run Gazetta from `main`](https://github.com/gazetta-studio/gazetta-studio#quick-start).

# Command line

Every `gazetta` command, its arguments and flags, and how the CLI picks a site and a target. Run commands with `npx gazetta <command>` from the project, or through the `dev` script `gazetta init` adds to `package.json`. `npx gazetta help` (also `--help` or `-h`, or no command at all) prints a short version of this page.

## Commands at a glance

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `gazetta init [dir]` | Create a new project and install its dependencies (`--no-install` skips the install) |
| `gazetta dev [site]` | Run the site and the admin at `http://localhost:3000` |
| `gazetta publish [target] [site]` | Render the site and write it to a target |
| `gazetta serve [target] [site]` | Serve a target's published pages |
| `gazetta build [site]` | Build the admin for `gazetta admin` |
| `gazetta admin [site]` | Run the built admin without the dev server |
| `gazetta deploy [target] [site]` | Run the target's deploy adapter |
| `gazetta validate [site]` | Check the site for broken references and other problems |
| `gazetta targets [site]` | Show what each target keeps and can do |
| `gazetta translate <item> --to <locale> [target]` | Copy a page or fragment as a new language version |
| `gazetta history [target] [site]` | List a target's revisions |
| `gazetta undo [target] [site]` | Restore the revision before the latest one |
| `gazetta rollback <rev> [target] [site]` | Restore a chosen revision |
| `gazetta assets <list\|info\|reindex> ...` | Inspect assets and rebuild dependency indices |
| `gazetta archive <list\|purge\|restore\|rename> ...` | Archive operations on pages and fragments |
| `gazetta agents update` | Refresh Gazetta's section of `AGENTS.md` from the installed package |
| `gazetta help` | Print the built-in help |

Any other command prints "Unknown command" and the help, and exits 1. The CLI looks for the site first, so where it finds none, or several, you get that error or question instead.

## Choosing the site and target

Arguments in square brackets are optional. The CLI fills them in:

**Site.** A `[site]` argument can be a site directory (`sites/main`), a name under `sites/` (`main`), or a project root that contains `sites/main`. Without one, the CLI uses the current directory if it has a `site.config.ts` (or `.js`, `.mjs`); otherwise it looks in `sites/`. One site there is used as is; with several, you're asked to choose. With none, the command stops and suggests `gazetta init`.

**Target.** For `publish`, `serve`, `deploy`, `history` and `undo`, and for `rollback` after its revision, the target argument is read as a site when it contains a `/` or is a directory with a site config; otherwise it's the target name. The other commands take the target first and the site after it. Without a target, these six commands use a site's only target (`publish` then stops: it needs a second target to publish to), and on a site with several they ask you to choose. The other commands use the editing target (below). So name the target in scripts:

```bash
npx gazetta publish staging
npx gazetta publish production sites/main
```

**Editing target.** Commands that read or change content (`publish` as the source, `dev`, `admin`, `validate`, `assets`, `archive`, `translate` without a target) use the first editable target in `site.config.ts`. A site with no editable target stops with an error that shows how to mark one; see [Targets](/docs/targets).

## Ports and addresses

`dev`, `serve` and `admin` listen on port 3000. Change it with `--port <n>` or `-p <n>`. If the port is taken, the command says so and exits 1.

| Command | Listens on by default |
|---|---|
| `gazetta dev` | `127.0.0.1` only: it serves the admin API, and without auth anyone who reaches it is an admin |
| `gazetta admin` | `127.0.0.1` while `admin.auth` is `trust: 'none'` (the default); every interface when real auth is configured |
| `gazetta serve` | every interface: it serves only the site, as a container does |

`--host <address>` (or `--host=<address>`) overrides this, for example `npx gazetta dev --host 0.0.0.0` to open the site from a phone on the same network. `--host` on any other command is an error. See [Authentication and authorization](/docs/auth) before exposing the admin.

## Commands

### `gazetta init [dir]`

Creates a project in `dir` (default: the current directory), then runs `npm install` in it. It refuses when `dir` already has a `sites/` folder or a `site.config.ts`. If `npm install` fails, the files stay in place, npm's error is shown, and the command exits 1; run `npm install` in the project yourself to finish. The new site depends on a range of the CLI's own version. With `--no-install`, `init` writes the project without running npm and ends by telling you to run `npm install`, for example to install offline later or with pnpm or yarn. [Getting started](/docs) walks through it.

`init` also writes an `AGENTS.md` with a section for coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Cursor). It tells the agent to install the Gazetta skill, which ships in the package at `node_modules/gazetta/agents/gazetta/`, into the folder its client reads skills from. The skill covers editing pages, fragments and translations, writing templates and schemas, and `gazetta validate`. It also lists the commands and admin routes an agent must never run itself (publishing, deploying, undo and rollback, purging, and deleting pages, fragments or assets) and must ask you about instead. Nothing enforces that list: on your own machine, only the agent and your agent client's own settings stop it. If `dir` already has an `AGENTS.md`, `init` adds the section at the end and leaves your text as it is. If it has a `CLAUDE.md`, `init` adds an `@AGENTS.md` import line to it, because Claude Code reads `AGENTS.md` only when a project has no `CLAUDE.md`.

The section and the skill carry the Gazetta version they came with; the section tells the agent to reinstall the skill when its installed copy is older. An existing project gets them, or a newer copy after upgrading Gazetta, with [`gazetta agents update`](#gazetta-agents-update).

### `gazetta dev [site]`

Runs the site at `http://localhost:3000/` and the admin at `/admin`, rendering pages from the editing target on each request. It watches templates, content and `site.config.ts`, and reloads the preview when they change; a `site.config.ts` change (content, locales, targets) takes effect without a restart. Two cases still need a restart: changes to `admin.hooks`, `admin.validators` or `admin.routes`, and a target's storage once the admin has published through it, because publish providers are created once and reused (#1446). At start it prints the pages, fragments and a Settings block, plus a line suggesting `gazetta agents update` when your `AGENTS.md` has an older Gazetta section, or none (project, site, templates, editing target); set `GAZETTA_QUIET=1` to leave the Settings block out. Flags: `--port`, `--host`. Stop it with Ctrl+C.

### `gazetta publish [target] [site]`

Renders the site and writes it to the target, copying from the editing target. Only pages and fragments whose content, template or dependencies changed since the last publish to that target are written; the output says how many were skipped as unchanged.

| Flag | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--force`, `-f` | Publish every item, without checking what changed |

It stops before writing anything when the site has only one target ("nowhere to publish to"), when the target is the editing target itself, when the target doesn't exist, or when a template is invalid. It exits 1 when any item or target fails. The whole flow, the admin's Publish panel, and what the CLI doesn't do yet (choose a source, pick items, remove items) are in [Publishing](/docs/publishing).

### `gazetta serve [target] [site]`

Serves a target's published output from its storage at `http://localhost:3000/`, the way a self-hosted server or container runs the site. It serves the site only, not the admin. A `static` target is served as files; a `dynamic` target has its pages assembled from fragments on each request. Flags: `--port`, `--host`. See [Self-hosted](/docs/self-hosted).

### `gazetta build [site]`

Builds the admin into `dist/admin/` at the project root, and bundles the custom editors and fields in `admin/editors/` and `admin/fields/` with it. `gazetta admin` serves this folder. Run it again after changing an editor or field.

### `gazetta admin [site]`

Runs the admin from `dist/admin/` at `http://localhost:3000/admin`, without the dev server or file watching. It stops with "admin UI not built" until `gazetta build` has run. Flags: `--port`, `--host`.

### `gazetta deploy [target] [site]`

Runs the deploy adapter set as the target's `deploy:` field, for example the Cloudflare Worker. Deploy and publish are separate: deploy puts the runtime in place, publish writes the content. A target without `deploy:` stops with an example of how to add one. Exits 1 when the adapter fails. See [Deploy](/docs/deploy) and [Cloudflare](/docs/cloudflare).

### `gazetta validate [site]`

Checks every page and fragment for broken references (templates, fragments, assets), content that doesn't match its template's schema, and site config problems, plus custom editors without a template and fields a schema names that don't exist in `admin/fields/`. A template that exists but fails to load (a syntax error, a failing import, no `schema` export) is an error, named once with its load error; each page and fragment using it also gets an error saying its content can't be checked.

Content that doesn't fit its template's schema (a required field missing, a value of the wrong type) is an error here, so the run fails until the content is fixed. Each issue is listed under its page or fragment with the field, the component and the language version. Site health in the admin shows the same problems as warnings.

To check a template change in a pull request, run it with `--base`: see [Check a template change in CI](/docs/templates#check-a-template-change-in-ci) for a workflow to copy.

| Flag | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--severity <level>` | What to show and count: `error` (default), `warn` (errors and warnings) or `all` (also info) |
| `--include-quality` | Also render each page and run the accessibility, HTML validity and broken-link checks. Slower |
| `--no-warn-as-error` | Don't fail the run on warnings (with `--severity=warn` or `all`) |
| `--verbose`, `-v` | Also list each warning and info item; errors are always listed |
| `--base <ref>` | Fail only on problems the commit `<ref>` (for example `origin/main`) didn't have. Its content is checked against its own templates, and the problems it already had are listed apart as "already broken", at the severities `--severity` shows. A problem counts as already broken when it's on the same item, language, component and field, and about the same thing (the missing reference, the broken link, the rule or the config setting), even if the message reads differently. `<ref>` must be a commit git can find; exit code 2 otherwise |
| `--targets <a,b>` | Also check the content stored on the named targets, with the working tree's templates (and, with `--base`, the base commit's). Each problem there says how to fix it: publish the target's content back to the editing target, fix it in the PR, and publish again. CI needs each target's read credentials, the same ones `gazetta publish` uses. On a static target, missing fragments aren't checked: its fragments are baked into its pages at publish, so it stores none, and the repo's own check covers them. An empty list, a name that isn't a target, a public target (it holds no manifests) or a target that can't be read, or doesn't answer within 10 seconds, stops the run with exit code 2; no target is skipped |
| `--render` | Also render the pages and fragments, in every language, that use a template changed since `--base` (directly or through a fragment), as publish renders them, writing nothing; a template that throws is an error naming the item, language and template. Without `--base`, everything is rendered, which is slow on a large site. A static target named with `--targets` isn't rendered: it stores no fragments to render its pages with. Without `--render`, no template runs |
| `--json` | Print the report as one JSON document on stdout, and everything else on stderr. Same as `--format json` |
| `--format github` | For GitHub Actions: append a job summary (a table per template) to the file `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` names, or print it when that's unset, and print one annotation per broken template on its entry file |

The JSON report:

| Field | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `ok` | Whether the run passes, as the exit code says |
| `counts` | `error`, `warn` and `info`: every issue found, whether `--severity` lists it or not |
| `templates` | One entry per template with problems, by name: `template`, `file` (its entry file, such as `templates/hero/index.tsx`), `issues` (problems with the template itself) and `items` |
| `other` | Problems that belong to no template, such as a missing fragment, a site config issue or an orphaned editor, by item or file |
| `alreadyBroken` | With `--base`: the problems `<ref>` already had that `--severity` shows, as `templates` and `other`. They don't count toward `ok` or `counts` |

Each item has `kind` (`page` or `fragment`), `name`, `locale` (`null` for the default language), `target` (`null` for the repo, or the target's name), `fix` (for a target's item with a new problem, how to fix it) and `issues`. Each issue has `validator`, `severity`, `message`, `component` (the component's path in the item) and `contentPath` (the field in its content, such as `cta`).

Exit code: 0 when the run passes, 1 when there are errors, and 2 when `--base` or `--targets` can't be used (a commit git can't find, a target that can't be checked). With `--severity=warn` or `all`, warnings fail the run too, unless `--no-warn-as-error` is set; with the default `--severity=error`, a run with only warnings reports "All good." and exits 0. Site config issues and the template, editor and field checks are shown whatever `--severity` is.

### `gazetta targets [site]`

Prints every target in `site.config.ts` with what it keeps and can do: whether its storage is public or private and why, whether it keeps history, where its audit events are kept, whether content review and scheduling are available, whether publishing to it needs approval and from how many people, whether it can serve redirects and `410 Gone`, whether it keeps dependency indices, and its deploy adapter. These are the rows of "About this target" in the admin's target menu. It reads the config only and connects to no storage, and exits 0. See [Targets](/docs/targets).

### `gazetta translate <item> --to <locale> [target]`

Copies a page or fragment manifest as a new language version, for example:

```bash
npx gazetta translate pages/about --to fr
```

writes `pages/about/page.fr.json`, which you then edit. `<item>` starts with `pages/` or `fragments/`; `<locale>` is a language code such as `fr` or `pt-br` (`--to=fr` also works). It works on the named target, or the first editable target, and refuses when the language version already exists. See [Pages and fragments](/docs/pages-and-fragments).

### `gazetta history [target] [site]`

Lists a target's revisions, newest first, with each one's id, operation, time and items. `--limit <n>` sets how many (default 50). On a target with `history: { enabled: false }` the command stops and says history is off.

### `gazetta undo [target] [site]`

Restores the target to the revision before its latest one, as a new revision. On a target with `environment: 'production'` it asks for confirmation; `--yes` (`-y`) skips the question.

### `gazetta rollback <rev> [target] [site]`

Restores a chosen revision, by the id `gazetta history` shows (`rev-...`), as a new revision. Production targets ask for confirmation as `undo` does.

On a publish destination, `undo` and `rollback` restore the content files but don't re-render the pages, so the live site doesn't change yet; see [Publishing](/docs/publishing#destination-undo-does-not-change-served-pages-yet).

### `gazetta assets list|info|reindex`

```text
gazetta assets list [target] [site]
gazetta assets info <name> [target] [site]
gazetta assets reindex [target] [site]
```

`list` shows the assets on an editable target; `info` shows one asset's details, variants, language and theme versions, and where it's used; `reindex` rebuilds the dependency indices (which pages use which fragments and assets) from the manifests, for example after editing content outside the admin. Stop the dev server before reindexing. The target defaults to the editing target and must be editable. See [Content assets](/docs/content-assets).

### `gazetta archive list|purge|restore|rename`

```text
gazetta archive list [--kind=page|fragment] [target] [site]
gazetta archive purge <name> [--kind=...] [--force] [target] [site]
gazetta archive restore <name> [--kind=...] [target] [site]
gazetta archive rename <oldname> <newname> [--kind=...] [--no-keep-alias] [--force] [target] [site]
```

Lists, permanently deletes and restores archived pages and fragments, and renames a live one, on an editable target, the same operations as the admin. `rename` keeps a redirect from the old name; `--no-keep-alias` drops it, and `--keep-alias` restores the default after an earlier `--no-keep-alias`. `--kind` is only needed when a page and a fragment share the name. See [Soft delete](/docs/soft-delete#cli).

### `gazetta agents update`

Refreshes the Gazetta section of the project's `AGENTS.md` from the installed package: only the text between the `gazetta:agents` start and end markers changes, and your own text around it stays as it is. Without a section, it adds one at the end; without an `AGENTS.md`, it creates one. If the project has a `CLAUDE.md` without an `@AGENTS.md` line, it adds one. It writes nothing in your agent client's folders: ask your agent to reinstall the skill from `node_modules/gazetta/agents/`. It prints what changed, or that the section is already current, and exits 0. Run it inside the project; outside one (no `package.json` depending on `gazetta`) it exits 2.

## In CI

The CLI treats any non-empty `CI` environment variable (GitHub Actions and most CI systems set `CI=true`) as non-interactive:

- It never asks a question. Where it would ask you to choose a site or target, it stops with an error listing the choices, so pass them as arguments.
- `undo` and `rollback` on a production target need `--yes`.
- `.env` and `.env.local` aren't loaded; set the variables in the CI environment.

Output has no colours when `NO_COLOR` is set or the output isn't a terminal.

## Environment files

Outside CI, every command except `init` loads `.env` and then `.env.local`, first from the project root and then from the site directory, before reading `site.config.ts`. A variable already set in the environment, or in a file loaded earlier, is kept. `site.config.ts` reads them as `process.env.NAME`; see [Targets](/docs/targets) for secrets.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | Success, or you cancelled a question (choosing a site or target, confirming an undo) |
| `1` | Anything failed: an unknown command or target, a missing site, a failed publish item or target, validation errors, a port in use, a failed deploy |
| `2` | `gazetta agents update` was run outside a project, or with other arguments |

`dev`, `serve` and `admin` keep running until you stop them with Ctrl+C.
